headline: Foot Locker deal lifts sales and profit; guidance raised
summary_short: DICK'S Sporting Goods reported net sales of $5.16B (+62.7% y/y, including $1.79B from the newly consolidated Foot Locker business) and net income of $319.8M ($3.54 diluted EPS), which included $131.2M of net litigation-settlement income and $73.5M of net Foot Locker acquisition charges.
summary_long: Net sales rose 62.7% y/y to $5.16B, including $1.79B from Foot Locker (acquired September 2025) and 6.0% comparable-sales growth at the DICK'S Business, driven by a 5.5% rise in sales per transaction. Gross margin fell 411bp on Foot Locker's lower-margin mix and a $42.7M Foot Locker inventory write-down; SG&A absorbed $480.4M of Foot Locker costs, partially offset by $174.5M of interchange-litigation and lease-termination settlement income. GAAP operating income rose to $450.7M from $366.1M; net income was $319.8M ($3.54 diluted EPS), including $73.5M of net acquisition-related charges. Cash was $998.2M; capex totaled $360.7M; the company paid a $1.25/share dividend and repurchased $141.2M of stock. Management raised its FY2026 comparable-sales outlook, guiding to $22.1-22.4B revenue and $13.27-14.27 diluted EPS.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes results to continued DICK'S momentum plus early Foot Locker turnaround progress, balanced against a dynamic tariff and macroeconomic backdrop.
Growth reflects $1.79B of newly consolidated Foot Locker net sales plus 6.0% DICK'S comparable-sales growth (5.5% higher ticket, 0.5% more transactions) and new-store openings.

Margin fell 411bp as Foot Locker carries structurally lower gross margin (-292bp) plus a $42.7M acquisition-related inventory write-down (-83bp); DICK'S own margin slipped 36bp on mix and higher shipping costs.

GAAP operating income rose to $450.7M as $174.5M of litigation and lease-termination settlement income offset $96.5M of Foot Locker acquisition-related costs (inventory write-down plus merger/integration charges).
Mirrors the operating-income drivers above; EBIT adds back $13.2M of net other income relative to GAAP operating income.
Mirrors the EBIT drivers plus $153.8M of quarterly depreciation and amortization added back.

Driven by settlement income and Foot Locker consolidation, partly offset by $73.5M of net acquisition charges and a higher 28.3% effective tax rate (vs 24.0% a year ago) from unrealized Foot Locker foreign-jurisdiction tax losses.
Diluted EPS growth trailed net income growth because 9.6 million shares issued to fund the Foot Locker acquisition diluted weighted-average diluted shares to 90.4 million from 81.5 million.
Basic EPS growth (+8.4%) trailed net income growth (+21.0%) because weighted-average basic shares rose to 88.5 million from 79.3 million, mainly reflecting the Foot Locker stock issuance.
